title: Reviewer-editor: the four Wave-1 plans whose quality gates cannot detect bad work
next_step: A DIFFERENT fresh reviewer-editor must judge each of the four edited versions. PLAN-LOOP.md rule 1: an agent may approve the version it received or materially edit it, never both. All four are now awaiting-recriticism and NONE is dispatchable to a builder.

outcome_per_plan.W1-15: MATERIAL EDIT. Zero human gates anywhere in a feel system. Added a played gate (two bounded routes, <=10 min driven play per route per arm) asking RI-STL01 section 3's own question - can you read the dark from the screen rather than a meter - with an ablated interior-lighting null arm that must be judged worse, a stated effect size and worst-site binding. Also added the Builder/critic execution allocation section PLAN-LOOP.md rule 3a requires and the received plan entirely lacked, which the audit did not catch.
outcome_per_plan.W1-12: MATERIAL EDIT. Added step 8a, a played fight quality gate riding on fixtures step 3 already builds, with the deleted-repair null arm section 4 already requires. Steps 8 and 9 kept VERBATIM and reclassified as mechanism/leak checks: I read RI-AI01 and RI-AI05 and both chart packs are transcribed correctly from the items, so the defect is the corpus's, not the plan's.
outcome_per_plan.W1-09: MATERIAL EDIT, and I disagree with part of the audit. Added step 2a, a played-and-watched fight gate riding on the RI-CMB07 M2-CTRL fights already required. But the 55 runnable-weight denominator is native RI-CMB07 text and it removes M1 Mode-A replay and M2-LIVE seam debt - an instrument row and a dependency row, NOT the quality read. The blind pair carries zero scoring weight in that item, so it was never in any denominator to renormalise away. Corrected in the plan so the next reader does not re-derive it. Also made the item's narrow renormalisation exception explicit, because step 3's blanket ban and the RI-CMB07 row did genuinely contradict each other in the same document.
outcome_per_plan.W1-08: MATERIAL EDIT, one clause. W1-29's closure clause copied with the operative fragment intact. NO new human gate added and none needed: RI-JRN03's JC-03N naive pass is already a fresh person playing the shipping game for fifteen minutes and answering quality questions in their own words. That row is sound and pieces lacking one should copy it.

corpus_findings_not_patched: RI-JRN03 scoring: weights 28+26+10+12+14+10 = 100 with Naive corroboration at 10 against a >=90 Meets band. A build whose fresh players could not work out the controls scores 90/100 and Meets. Native to the item; the hard fails (HF10/M-N5, M-N4>=2, M-N7>=3) catch only catastrophe, not a merely unguessable scheme. Repaired at plan-closure level as W1-29 does, not by editing the bar.

RI-AI01:252 and RI-AI05:276 build their blind counterpart from their own published design tables. RI-CMB07's wave-1 amendment (BAR-CRITIQUE-W1-09-R1 section R5) rules exactly that VOID: 'a pack whose counterpart is generated from section D, from this item's text, or from any published design table is VOID'. Two items in corpus/10-combat/ disagree. Needs an ARBITRATION ruling, not a plan edit.

RI-STL01, RI-STL02, RI-CRM01, RI-CRM02 all declare blind_pair: no. The corpus supplies W1-15 no human read of any kind. blind_pair: no forbids an A/B pack, not a played session, so the plan gate is legitimate - but the bar-level gap is real and belongs to a corpus owner.

RI-CMB09 M7 is a STILL pair asking 'which of these two characters is out of breath?'. That is Ruling W2's named falsifier case - a frozen pose genuinely is the artefact - so it is left unchanged. Recorded because the audit's cross-cutting pattern (b) would otherwise sweep it up.
what_i_could_not_do: I ran no browser, no GPU pod and no game. This was a text round, per PLAN-LOOP.md's cheap-first discipline. Every claim above is from the plans, the four sets of reference items, and the presence of named tools on disk.

I did not regenerate orchestration/INDEX.md. Its own header says GENERATED by tools/gen-index.mjs, do not edit. I added no tool and no reference item, so regenerating from this worktree would only restamp it - and HAZARDS.md section 2d is explicit that staging a file from a tree that is stale for another agent's pushed work is the single largest source of lost work found so far. This task appears in INDEX's 'In flight right now' table through its own status file, which is how that table is built.

I did not verify that the four played gates are actually executable end to end - that a fresh agent can in fact drive a theft, a fight and an escape through the shipping build today. Each gate names existing instruments by path and each path exists, but whether the driven-play protocol works is a build-time question and a builder is REQUIRED to report it as a plan defect the moment it does not (PLAN-LOOP.md, 'a plan must never become a commitment device').

I did not audit the other twenty-six plans. The audit's ranked list items 4-8 (W1-01, W1-27, W1-16, W1-22, and the stale reference premise in W1-24/W1-06/W1-03) are untouched by this round and W1-01 remains the audit's highest-value outstanding item - it is satisfied and dispatchable TODAY against predicates Ruling W1 overturned.
weakest_joints_in_my_own_edits: W1-15: the ablation disconnects the interior lighting consumer. If that reads as obviously broken rather than less legible, it is the trivial wrong answer, not the plausible one - HAZARDS.md section 0's exact failure shape. Named in the plan for the next reviewer to rule on.

W1-12 and W1-09: both null arms reuse a delete-the-fix copy the plan already builds, which is cheap and honest but couples the quality gate to one specific repair. If the repair is small enough that a player cannot feel it, the gate reports 'inert' and blocks closure on a technicality. Named in both plans; I did not pre-empt the call.

W1-08: I bound the closure clause on all seven M-N thresholds where W1-29 says only 'independent naive pass'. That is stricter than the clause I copied, and two of the seven depend on world content W1-08 does not own. Named in the plan with the looser alternative (bind on M-N1, the item's own headline naive number, plus the hard fails).
